claims.text: The interaction between thwarted belongingness and perceived burdensomeness is significantly associated with suicidal ideation.
The interaction between thwarted belongingness, perceived burdensomeness, and capability for suicide is significantly related to a greater number of prior suicide attempts.
Effect sizes for the interpersonal theory interaction pathways are modest.
Alternative configurations of interpersonal theory variables are similarly useful for predicting suicide risk as theory-consistent pathways.

evidence.description: Meta-analyses across 122 distinct samples showed that the interaction between thwarted belongingness and perceived burdensomeness was significantly associated with suicidal ideation.

Meta-analyses across 122 distinct samples demonstrated that the interaction between thwarted belongingness, perceived burdensomeness, and capability for suicide was significantly related to a greater number of prior suicide attempts.
Random-effects meta-analytic evaluation revealed modest effect sizes for the posited theoretical interaction pathways.
Meta-analytic comparisons indicated that alternative configurations of theoretical constructs predicted suicide risk with similar utility to theory-consistent pathways.

methodologies.name: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
methodologies.description: Hypothesis-driven systematic review and random-effects meta-analyses of published and unpublished literature evaluating interpersonal theory constructs.

limitations.text: Effect sizes for key interpersonal theory interactions were modest.
Theory-consistent interaction pathways do not outperform alternative configurations of the same theoretical variables in predicting suicide risk.
